title: Band loyalty, bassist Dan LeBlanc and guitarist Arthur Ponce
summary: He talks about taking any work to keep the men employed, bassist Dan LeBlanc, and guitarist Arthur Ponce, a phone call, and Ponce's arrangements.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Oh, listen, musicians, there's a rule of regulars. Take it from me. I know my band, I can show you pictures where they're laughing and they're jolly and they all love one another. And they love their leader in spite of what people think. But they used to try to put me on in lots of ways. I remember I used to, as I tell you, I would take anything to make money and keep them busy. Because my bass player, I had a great bass player named Dan LeBlanc, he died prematurely. He told me one night we would play with you because you get to work. And I said, isn't there any sentiment attached to you guys? Don't you feel that I'm a good guy and that you could depend on me to get you out of jail?
I had the greatest musicians in this world in my band. I mean in this world. Now that's taken a lot of territory. I had Arthur Ponce, guitarist. Do you know him?
Did you ever have him play?
As near as I could tell. He called me the other night. He said, Dad. Oh, loud too.
